title: LANDSCAPE of the Homeless
author: Dola Dutta Roy
text:
The little abode
of sticks and straw,
In the parlor of a dry desert land,
was home to me and my own.

It stands today,
shell-shocked;
with the blood
of my babies,
splattered across!

The pomegranate trees
stand charred,
and the fruits are quashed
in terror.
Nothing but the signature
of an inane game --
they call `war`.

My breath wanders like a spirit,
embalming the swelling corpses,
that have no names.
No faces left.

With every fall,
vultures whisper
of a feast,
they know they cannot digest.
The cry of Mother Earth rises,
but there`s no one to hear her groan.
And humanity remains silent.

was home to me and my own.
My breath wanders like a spirit,
The cry of Mother Earth rises,
but there`s no one to hear her groan.
